:::{#thm-hessian-quadratic}
#### Hessian of a quadratic form

If $\matr{S}$ is a symmetric $p \times p$ matrix that is constant with respect to $\vx$,
then $f(\vx) = \tp{\vx} \matr{S} \vx$ has $\matr{H}_f(\vx) = 2 \matr{S}$ for every $\vx$.

:::

::: proof

$$
\ba
\matr{H}_f(\vx)
&= \deriv{\vx} \tp{\paren{\deriv{\vx} (\tp{\vx} \matr{S} \vx)}}
&& \text{(@def-hessian)}
\\
&= \deriv{\vx} \tp{\paren{2 \matr{S} \vx}}
&& \text{(@thm-quadratic-form)}
\\
&= \paren{\deriv{\vx} \vx}\,\tp{(2 \matr{S})}
&& \text{(@thm-deriv-matrix-vector, with } \matr{A} = 2 \matr{S} \text{ and } \vecf{v} = \vx \text{; } \deriv{\vx} \tp{(2 \matr{S} \vx)} = \deriv{\vx} (2 \matr{S} \vx) \text{, @def-vector-valued-derivative)}
\\
&= \matr{I}_p\,\tp{(2 \matr{S})}
&& \text{(} \deriv{\vx} \vx = \matr{I}_p \text{, @rem-deriv-matrix-vector-special-case)}
\\
&= 2 \matr{S}.
&& \text{(} \matr{S} \text{ is symmetric)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-hessian-quadratic}
#### The Hessian of a $2 \times 2$ quadratic form

For $\matr{S} = \sbmat{ 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 }$ as in @exm-deriv-quadratic-form,
@thm-hessian-quadratic gives $\matr{H}_f(\vx) = \sbmat{ 6 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 }$.
Directly, the gradient found there, with $\coef{i}$ renamed $x_i$, is $\tp{(6 x_1 + 2 x_2,\ 2 x_1 + 4 x_2)}$,
and differentiating its entries by $x_1$ and by $x_2$ (@def-hessian) gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\matr{H}_f(\vx)
&= \sbmat{
\deriv{x_1} (6 x_1 + 2 x_2) & \deriv{x_1} (2 x_1 + 4 x_2) \\
\deriv{x_2} (6 x_1 + 2 x_2) & \deriv{x_2} (2 x_1 + 4 x_2)
} \\
&= \sbmat{ 6 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 }.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
